newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - IPE BRENT TO RECOVER, WEEKLY CHART POSITIVE.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - IPE BRENT TO RECOVER, WEEKLY CHART POSITIVE.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
* Brent set to continue lower with July 14's $17.86 low the next target and stiff resistance around $18.63-79. Weekly chart more constructive.
* Brent will be looking for some consolidation from support in the $18.20-40 range to keep in touch with the recent up trend.

IPE Brent crude and gas oil may recover Friday's losses with short-covering following Friday's sell-off steadying the market on Monday. But both must hold support to ensure the longer term uptrend stays intact, analysts said.
Brent will lookfor some consolidation from support in the $18.20-40 range to keep in touch with the recent up trend.

The market closed below the short-term uptrend support stemming from July 15's $17.80 low on the spot month chart, but longer term uptrend support from June 11's $17.32 trough remains intact and comes in at around $18.30 today.

Peter Sceats at CharTec-MCS said, "A further fall below trend support would be a classic technical forecast but the September chart carries less and less technical weight the closer it comes to expiry".
Momentum indicators, mostly showing the market oversold but analysts say this could be corrected early this week as short positions are covered back following Friday's sell off.

On Friday the September contract dipped below long term downtrend support from May 20's $20.40 which forms the second leg of a double top started on May 16. But it closed well above this and support is now around $18.40 on the September chart.

Nicola Merrell analyst at MMS International in London took a more bearish view. "The market looks set to continue lower with $July 14's $17.86 low the next target and some siff resistance around $18.63-79 to the upside".
She said stochastic indicators looked very weak after crossing on Thursday and continued to point the market lower.

However, some analysts said that despite Friday's losses the outlook remained positive and if the market can hold $18.40 support there may still be room for it to break back above $19 in the longer term. Some even thought the $19.60 barrier would be cleared eventually and the market would trade just below $20.
Peter Sceats said "Looking at the weekly chart depicts a somewhat more constructive technical profile. Despite the down close on Friday the price is still the right side of uptrend support".
"On the right side of the line we have an ongoing upwave, but a break south of the line and the bearish background technicals, a medium term down trend, should push prices lower," Sceats added.
Gas oil gapped bearishly lower on Friday . Following the "exhaustion gap" formed at the beginning of last week gas oil has traded successively lower.

It has put in a small 25 cent gap down Wednesday to Thursday, when it closed below trendline support, and a wide gap down from Thursdays $172 low to Friday's $171 high, which analysts say could prove difficult to fill for a while.
However, they said a combination of other measures are becoming supportive and could put a base in the market around $168 as the trend turns generally lower.

These include continuing diverging of the 10 and 20-day moving average lines and RSI's which are starting to flag an oversold market, though falling stochastics line are still pointing the market lower.
The September chart shows a similar pattern of trade though support comes in at around $169.25 the low of July 31.
--Colin Wooster, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7456
